overview: Systematic review of observational and intervention studies of relational continuity with a family physician and unplanned hospital admissions in adults aged 65 and over.
population: Studies of adults aged 65 and over registered in primary care in high-income health systems.
exposure: Relational continuity measured by a validated index (usual provider, Bice-type or sequential measures), or an intervention designed to raise it.
procedures: Search three bibliographic databases from 2000, with forward citation checking of included studies and a check of every scan lead. Two reviewers screen independently; the third resolves disagreements. Extraction includes the continuity index, adjustment set and follow-up. Risk of bias is assessed with a tool for non-randomised studies, with severity adjustment as a key domain.

outcomes.name: Unplanned hospital admission
outcomes.measure: Adjusted rate ratio or hazard ratio for highest against lowest continuity, as reported
outcomes.timing: Follow-up of at least one year
outcomes.why: The outcome the network hopes to reduce.

feasibility: About 40 hours per reviewer covers an expected 2,000 records and 25 to 35 included studies.

biasFlags.label: Confounding by severity in included studies
Reviewers with a stake in the decision

parsimony.simplestPath: One outcome, severity-adjusted estimates only, intervention studies apart.

theoreticalFramework: None; the review question is empirical.
summary: Review protocol with severity adjustment as a condition for pooling and waits as a balancing outcome.
